articles.title: US President Donald Trump says deportation policy was 'too tough' for voters
articles.summary: Trump said his deportation policy may be one of the reasons the Republicans lost so much ground in the midterm elections.

image.caption: Donald Trump said can he can work with Democrats on some kind of immigration dealImage: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said that his deportation policy for undocumented immigrants was "too tough" for voters and he can work with the Democrats in the new Congress to craft an immigration deal.

Speaking during his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm election, Trump said his deportation policy may have been part of the reason Republicans lost.
"I think it was too tough," Trump said. "I think it might be too tough, yeah. And a lot of people would say that it’s great. But a lot of people think it’s too tough."
In his interview to CBS that aired on Sunday, Trump said that he can find a way to work with the Democrats.
"The deal would be we would work something out. And I think it's something — I think that's something that's actually doable," he said in the interview.

Trump did not share the details of what the immigration deal would look like but shortly after the interview he appointed Stephen Miller, who designed the Trump administration's hardline deportation policy, as his chief of staff.
When ICE comes knocking: the fight against Trump's deportations
In his tenure, Trump's administration has aggressively pushed to deport millions of undocumented migrants which drew widespread criticism.
Trump 'only kidding' about Dana White press secretary job offer
Trump said he was just joking about making Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White his next White House press secretary.
"I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump told reporters.
In a social media post Saturday, Trump implored White to accept his offer, writing, "Dana, please take the job!" and calling him a "violent fighter and warrior."
White is a long-time friend of Trump. He has maintained silence on Trump's remarks, saying that he would "have more to talk about" after meeting with Trump on Monday.
The position of the press secretary has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week on the job.
Trump to meet Xi, Putin to end Iran war
Trump on Sunday said that he will be meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin ‌at an ⁠APEC ⁠leaders' summit in China next week to discuss ending the Iran war.

Before flying back to Washington from Florida, Trump while speaking to the media said: "One of the meetings, I think, will be with ‌President Putin and President Xi, and that'll be ‌interesting. ​We're talking a lot of things, including denuclearization, but we'll be talking a lot of things. We're trying to end the ​war in Iran."
Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached
Russia in October has said that this first of its kind trilateral meeting is "being prepared."
While Trump has mentioned denuclearization as the focus of the meeting, a Wall Street Journal report said that Putin wanted the three-way talks to broker a peace deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

In his interview with CBS Trump said that "I believe we're very close to ⁠making a ​deal" to end the Russia-Ukraine war that would result in a "little bit different shape Ukraine," without sharing any further details.

articles.title: Why citizens want special COA audit of Bacolod’s multi-billion peso loans
articles.summary: Religious and civil society groups want a probe into a P1.7 billion loan during the term of ex-mayor Evelio 'Bing' Leonardia and two deals worth a combined P6.2 billion under former mayor Alfredo…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY, Philippines – Public outcry continues to grow over the loan brouhaha in Bacolod City.
And it looks out of the ordinary now.

Religious and civil society groups have united to ask the Commission on Audit (COA) for a special audit of city projects funded by multi-billion peso loans and long-term obligations incurred during the terms of former mayors Evelio “Bing” Leonardia and Alfredo Abelardo “Albee” Benitez.

Standing together in deep alarm, the Joint Civil Society Coalition (JCSC) called for full transparency and public accountability by demanding an investigation into the city’s controversial financial obligations: the P1.7 billion loan under the Leonardia administration, and the P4.171 billion loan alongside an additional P2.1 billion service contract under Benitez’s term.
The demand for a special audit emerged amid rising tensions among city officials regarding local government loans and the controversial, unfinished P765-million legislative building.

blocks.caption: Benitez-Bais spat puts Bacolod’s stalled P765-M project, flood contractor in focus

blocks.text: In their four-page letter addressed to city and COA officials, released to the media on Friday, November 6, the coalition asked for the immediate online release of all signed loan contracts, repayment matrices, bank covenants, and long-term service agreements in an easily readable format for public perusal and evaluation.
The coalition also demanded a freeze on all further loan disbursements pending completion of COA’s audit and reevaluation of implemented projects.
Both Councilor Wilson Gamboa Jr. and Homer Bais spun the call for audit, especially the P4.171 billion loan from Development Bank of the Philippines by the previous Benitez’s mayoral administration.
Gamboa is a “lone wolf” on the city council, while Bais is a political ally of Benitez under local party Team Asenso.
However, it was Bais who was involved in an altercation with Benitez, which later escalated into a table-thumping incident in the lobby of the Bacolod City Government Center on October 16.
Five days after the infamous table-slamming incident, Benitez publicly apologized for conduct unbecoming a deputy speaker of the House.

blocks.caption: ‘Ti, ano kung Benitez ka?’: Bacolod allies nearly come to blows over city’s debts

blocks.text: A call for an audit of his multi-billion-peso loans and unfinished projects followed.
However, both Gamboa and Bais’ resolutions calling for an audit of Benitez’s loans and projects were voted down by the council majority in the council, which is politically allied with the latter.

Now comes the coalition of religious and civil society groups, with signatories saying they are making such a move not just as leaders of civil society organizations, faith communities, and professional associations, but as “deeply concerned taxpayers and residents who care for the welfare of the city and its inhabitants,” read a portion of the four-page coalition letter addressed to city and COA officials.

On October 30, anti-graft crusader John Chiong, founder and president of Task Force Kasanag (TFK), also requested COA Chairperson Gamaliela Cordoba to conduct a forensic audit on the loans and the legislative building being built by the controversial contractor, Legacy Construction Corporation, owned by Alex Abelido.

However, the coalition said that beyond multi-billion-peso bank loans for various development projects, the coalition also wants to know everything behind the P2.1-billion, 10-year agreement between the city and High Data Infrastructure Inc. (High Data) for the “Bacolod Super City” project.

Even though some councilors maintained that the contract with High Data is a Build-Transfer-Maintain (BTM) arrangement under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) rather than a loan, the coalition is alarmed that the city initially has to pay P125 million in 2025, followed by P200 million annually for the remaining nine years.
The ambitious P2.1 billion contract with High Data aims to build a smart communication infrastructure for a smart command center, leading the way to a Bacolod Super City.
The controversial billionaire gaming mogul, Benitez, is currently silent regarding the issues surrounding the city loans, the unfinished legislative building, and the High Data brouhaha.
In his press statement on October 19, the former mayor-turned-congressman said that he would continue to advocate for transparency and accountability in all government dealings.
However, when Bais proposed a resolution seeking a fraud audit from COA on the much-discussed legislative building on October 24, Albee kept mum.
His political allies in the council voted down Bais’s proposed resolution.

But the coalition said that for the city government to set aside P560 million in next year’s budget purely for loan principal and interest was an amount large enough to run an entire municipality or two.
It then asked: “By locking up annual funds for the decade-long contract deals, how will this burden benefit the people of Bacolod?”

The coalition reminded city executives that when billions are poured into public works and burdensome long-term contracts, it is the low-income families, informal settlers, public transport drivers, vendors, and small business owners who end up squeezed.

Worse, it added: “Future generations who had no voice in these deliberations will bear the weight of the debt servicing that swallows up a massive chunk of city revenues and essential funds for public health, education, flood control, other basic services, and vital development programs.”
“So, when the councilors step up to defend taxpayers and ask tough but necessary questions, they should be met with clear answers, not hostility,” the coalition reiterated.
“The Sangguniang Panlungsod cannot be a mere stamping pad,” it pointed out; it must exercise its responsibility to perform oversight duties when called for.

Thus, the coalition’s signatories stressed, “As the ones paying every single centavo spent on government projects, we demand full transparency, the highest standard of integrity, and accountability when warranted.”
Hence, it wants COA’s intervention by way of conducting a special audit covering the following:

items: all loan contracts
bank disbursements
interest schedules
construction timelines
long-term General Fund commitnents
project delays
financial slippage

blocks.text: The coalition said, “Government must balance the appetite for the high-impact initiatives against the needs of the most needy.”

articles.title: Resto in 'residential' land? Defense witness' answer draws senator-judge's ire
articles.summary: Senator-judge questions why a site housing Prime Bistro is described as residential.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 2:10pm
Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin testifies as the first defense witness in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate in Pasay City on Nov. 9, 2026.
The STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo accused Vice President Sara Duterte's first defense witness of "lying through his teeth" Monday, November 9 after he sought to explain why a property declared as residential could be a restaurant.
Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin was questioned about a property marked "910" on the city's property identification map that is occupied by Prime Bistro, a commercial establishment.
Adalin testified that the property covered by a Transfer Certificate of Title ending in 775 was the same property declared in Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
The vice president's SALN describes the property as a "residential lot," but the actual property is occupied by the restaurant.
Asked about the apparent discrepancy, Adalin said a building may appear commercial while actually being used for residential purposes.
"There are times na commercial ang building pero ang gamit is residential," Adalin said. ("There are times when a building is commercial but its use is residential.")
The explanation drew a sharp response from Tulfo.

"Nakalagay na nga 'yung Prime Bistro, commercial 'yun... Sabi niya commercial pero ginagamit residential. He's lying through his teeth na lumilitaw na para bang pinagloloko tayo," Tulfo said. ("It's clearly stated that Prime Bistro is commercial... He said it was commercial, but it's being used as residential. He's lying through his teeth, making it look as though he's taking us for fools.")

"So naglagay ka ng dining, naglagay ka ng karatula para tutulugan mo lang? Parang 'yun ang pinapalabas nitong witness," he added. ("So you set up a dining area, you put up a sign, just so you could sleep there? That seems to be what this witness is implying.")
Property in question
Prime Bistro is a Davao City restaurant on a property registered under Duterte's husband, lawyer Manases Carpio.
The National Bureau of Investigation previously cited the property among assets it was examining for alleged discrepancies in the couple's SALN declarations.

Records presented during the impeachment trial show that the property includes land with an assessed value of about P82,000 and a separate building. Tax declarations placed the combined market value of the land and building at roughly P9 million, while Duterte's SALN listed an acquisition cost of P10 million.

Adalin was called by the defense to testify about tax declarations and tax maps involving the Matina Crossing property and to support its position that the property had been disclosed in Duterte's SALN.

Article II, the sole remaining impeachment charge against Duterte, accuses her of amassing unexplained wealth, failing to fully and truthfully disclose her and her husband's assets in her SALNs, including those for 2022 to 2024, and failing to divest from business interests while serving as vice president from 2022 to 2025.
Duterte has denied the allegations.

articles.title: Jensen Huang: Silicon Valley superstar engulfed by personal scandal
articles.summary: Once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", Huang is mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
ByLily JamaliNorth America Technology correspondent and Peter HoskinsBusiness reporter
Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.
He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.
As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.
The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Who is Jensen Huang?
Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US.
He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.
Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.
He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.
Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.
Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.
"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".

blocks.caption: Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI Inc., from left, Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., US House Speaker Mike Johnson, a Republican from Louisiana, US President Donald Trump, Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), Nikesh…

blocks.text: Image source, Bloomberg via Getty Images
Huang has long found himself at the centre of US-China tensions. Trump has repeatedly said the two nations are in a race for dominance.
Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
Since 2022 the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

But it means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. In recent years Huang has engaged in a flurry of shuttle diplomacy, dashing between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.
Sunday's revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China.
Quarter after quarter of late, Nvidia has been locked out of that lucrative market. Despite his ostensible closeness to Trump, Huang has not managed to wrest this concession from the administration.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Huang is commonly referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan where he was born

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Huang is commonly referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan where he was born
What is Nvidia?
Huang founded Nvidia with fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993.
The company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games.
Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates.

"In 2012 these machine learning neural net researchers started to use it for that purpose and Jensen immediately recongnised that this was going to be a massive industry and the future of computing. He began to pour enormous amounts of resources into building what was essentially the AI hardware market," says Witt.

"Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them."
Nvidia is now worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.

"The first real neural net of modern times on an Nvidia network was Alex Krizhevsky's Alexnet and they trained that on two Nvidia cards in Alex's bedroom. Now we do the same thing but we do it with 200,000 - 300,000 cards and instead of doing it in a bedroom we do it in a giant barn full of computers called a data centre," adds Witt.

"So when you think about a data centre buildout, when you hear the AI infrastructure buildout, Jensen runs a tollbooth. All of that goes through him. And it made his company at least temporarily, the most valuable company in the world."
Nvidia's board has announced a probe following reports by the New York Times that Huang had engaged in a romantic relationship with a woman believed by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
For now, though, Nvidia's board appears to have little appetite for removing Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".
Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is also no clear successor to the 63-year old tech boss.
Who is Huang's wife?
Huang met his wife Lori at Oregon State University, where she was also studying electrical engineering and was his lab partner.
They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer.
He has credited Lori and Madison for making black leather jackets his signature style.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Lori Huang accompanied her husband at the state dinner held by President Donald Trump for his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in September

blocks.text: Lori Huang accompanied her husband at the state dinner held by President Donald Trump for his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in September
In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation.
The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.
Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.
"Jensen in my conversations with him and in other conversations has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man. That's very important to him," says Witt.

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways. Both of his children work for Nvidia. Spencer and Maddison. The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."
Huang for his part released a statement which said, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
What do we know about the alleged affair?
US officials had concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reports.

She was a top executive at Megaspeed, a data centre company based in Singapore. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.
Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.
Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.
When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.
"We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.
Additional reporting by Ayeshea Perera in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney

articles.title: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
articles.summary: The BBC enters Marseille's dangerous underworld, where young people are trapped, brutalised and exploited.

blocks.text: Warning: Strong language and descriptions of sexual violence
Although she had just bought hashish from a drug dealer, the woman decided to call the police.
It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022.
"We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read.
The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal.
One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings.
What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped.

Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived.

Arrests were made. Photos on the phone of one of the boys' alleged torturers showed several other young men in a similarly distressed condition. Six men have since been handed hefty sentences for what happened to the two teenagers.
The boys' story highlights the grip that drug gangs hold over parts of France's second city.
While the blend of Mediterranean culture, street art and hip-hop scene has made Marseille a popular tourist destination - beyond the city centre, it is another story.
After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly.
We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation.

We saw how gangs use social media to recruit hitmen and spoke to several young men caught up in the violence. From prison, one gang member accused of involvement in several murders explained how his "cold-bloodedness" had helped him rise through the ranks.
The city's most powerful gang, DZ Mafia, emerged victorious from a bloody turf war and is now one of the most feared criminal organisations in France.
DZ is the official internet country code for Algeria, where one of the gang's founders, a French-Algerian called Mehdi Laribi, was detained earlier this year under a French arrest warrant.

The criminal outfit rose to prominence in 2023, when it became the first French gang to capitalise on its notoriety by releasing video statements - using social media to market itself as a brand - says the head of the country's anti-drug trafficking unit, Dimitri Zoulas.
Its most recent statement came in July, when the mayor of a nearby town had to be placed in police protection, after intelligence suggested he was in danger of being targeted by the group.
In an online video, six masked men dressed in black stood behind a table - as one of them read a statement denying DZ Mafia's involvement.
France's expanding illegal drugs market - which has seen a surge in cocaine imports alongside high volumes of cannabis and synthetic drugs - has also helped the gang grow rapidly.

The number of cocaine users in France is expected soon to reach two million, says Zoulas, up from 600,000 in 2017. Drug smuggling across France generates €7bn (£5.9bn) a year, involving 200,000 people, he adds.

Many of those distributing the drugs are children and the authorities say the number of minors caught up in trafficking is increasing. During 2025, more than 10,000 children were involved in some way, according to official figures.
DZ Mafia is a prime example. To reach more customers, it needs more gang members - more children.
We have found it is now recruiting young people from across France - not just to sell drugs, but to carry out kidnap, torture and murder.
They are a generation seen as easy to corrupt, but also expendable, by the kingpins who typically control them from prison or overseas.
And, as police and judges warn, once these children enter Marseille's underworld, it is very hard to get them out.
Few know the human cost of Marseille's gangs like mother Karine Brouillard - who lives at the other end of France, almost as far from the Mediterranean coast as you can get.

Her son, Hugo, first ran away aged 15 - from his home in a village in the Nord department - after an argument with his family. He was picked up by police three days later, almost 1,000km (600 miles) away in Marseille, with money and cannabis on him. He was taken home.
But several years later, in 2023, Hugo planned to return south, telling his parents he had secured a holiday job at a restaurant near Marseille.
"He gave regular updates," Karine remembers. "He called me, everything was going well."
Three weeks later, a doctor called. Karine says she will never forget his words: "Your son arrived last night. He took a bullet to the head."
Police believe Hugo was brought for medical help from a gang-controlled area and suspect he was involved with one.
That area was Quartier Nord.
Our best way into Quartier Nord, where DZ Mafia wields power, is with the help of resident Fadella Ouidef, a 41-year-old mother-of-four who gives us a tour.
Thirty-seven seconds after entering one housing estate, we find ourselves cornered.

Car horns sound the moment Fadella's Peugeot passes a gang checkpoint - the teenagers manning the post immediately spot our camera. "Wait, stop filming," Fadella warns, as a grey 4x4 forces us to the side of the road.
"I'm making a report for my housing association," she tells the inquisitive driver. He eventually agrees to let us leave if we stop filming.
It is unnerving to see a non-police vehicle move so assertively and a relief to watch it leave.
"Lately, the gangs have been very aggressive," explains Fadella. "What we simply try to do is make sure our young people understand what's happening is wrong."
Fadella speaks to a wider fear among local families: that their children are enticed by huge sums of money to take a criminal path that robs them of their innocence.
Money is what led one young man to spend his teenage years with DZ Mafia.
In order for our interviewees to speak freely, or because of safety concerns, we have agreed to protect their identities.
Camil tells us he worked up the gang's ranks to "running security" in one area it controls.
The now 20-year-old, who claims to have left the group, is highly suspicious of our presence, but agrees to tell us how the gang recruits young members.
"They know how to get inside your head. Whatever you want, they give to you," he says. This can range from nice cars and spacious apartments, to drugs and prostitutes, he explains.
"You feel loyalty because of what they give you. You'll stay until the very end, until either death or prison."
Camil also gives a sobering assessment of what happens if the gang identifies a weakness in a recruit: "They'll exploit it. You're their bitch, it's over."
DZ Mafia member, Adam - not his real name - tells us he was part of a DZ Mafia hit squad when we speak to him in a Snapchat video call.
He is currently in prison awaiting trial, after being implicated in several murders.
"People noticed my determination, my cold-bloodedness and, without wanting to, I climbed up the ladder of the gang," says Adam. "It became my place, I had to roll with it."
During the chat, he agrees the killings he has been charged with were "quite shocking".

"Attempts in broad daylight, in traffic jams… it can range from going to hit a guy, slap him to taking him in front of his mother and burning him up in a car. I think I have good composure, I handle it fairly well."
We challenge Adam on whether he feels regret when carrying out such acts of brutality.
He says he is "feeling in-part guilty" but claims to have no regrets.
"If I hadn't done all of this, there are other people who would have done that in my place, and so on. I am just another brick in the wall," he says.
Like so many teenagers from Marseille, he knew large sums of money could be earned quickly in drug trafficking. Now in his twenties, he admits the environment he entered was a "trap".
At a so-called deal point in a social housing estate - sealed off and controlled by DZ Mafia - price lists for cocaine, hashish and marijuana are graffitied on a wall.
The estate acts as a natural fortress for drug dealers. With one major road in and out, they can control the flow of customers and see if the police are coming.
It is not uncommon for the sound of automatic gunfire to fill the night air in these areas.
After months of negotiations, a deal-point manager from a rival gang agrees to meet us where he works.
We enter the estate early in the morning, the birdsong and children walking to school providing a stark contrast to the industrial-scale criminal operation that takes place here.
"Joe" says he was making €3,000 (£2,500) a month when he was 13. Now he says that has risen to between €5,000 and €10,000 a month.
He seems to see his life path as pre-ordained, albeit a lucrative one.
We ask Joe if he thinks about the lives lost because of the violence carried out by his gang, but the 23-year-old has also long made peace with the pain and destruction drug trafficking can cause.
"It destroys people, but we all make our own choices," he shrugs.
The work that Joe's gang and DZ Mafia are doing represents a threat to national security, says Zoulas, of the anti-drug trafficking unit.
There are road accidents, as well as family violence, depressions, suicides and more than 700 overdoses each year, he says, "and it distorts the economy".
"We are heading towards a potential systemic breakdown of the criminal justice system."
Police have had success in Marseille and other cities against drug gangs.
Criminal operations are being frustrated, more kingpins arrested and drugs seized.
Since 2024, about 1,000 individuals associated with DZ Mafia have been arrested, and 600 incarcerated, police say.
But overall, it is a battle that is becoming more arduous, rather than easier.

As gangs seek to widen their operations, or replace members who have been arrested or killed, social media has become a potent recruitment tool - especially since the Covid pandemic, when many street-drug sales jumped online.
On social media, we found countless posts advertising jobs in Marseille for aspiring drivers, couriers and hitmen, often with glamourised AI-generated images.
Nets are also being cast wider, as it becomes harder to entice young people locally because they know more about what might happen to them.
The ads can reach teenagers in most corners of France - including Paris, Nantes and Lille - and serve as a powerful pull to Marseille, and the Quartier Nord, police say.
Online advertising has also changed the typical profile of someone who would join a gang's ranks, say law enforcement officials.
Now, it is often someone without a criminal past, but who has exploitable vulnerabilities, like having a difficult family life.
"These people are recruited by unscrupulous sponsors who send them into the lion's den," explains Thibaut Fontaine, the head of France's anti-organised-crime unit.
Their lack of criminal experience, he says, makes them easier to arrest quickly.
Karine still has no idea why her son, Hugo, was shot.

Asked what she would say to gang leaders recruiting children and young men in Marseille, she says: "They destroy families. Little sisters, little brothers, grandparents. But then, I don't think those people have a heart, really."
The restaurant where her son said he was going to work did exist, but staﬀ there told Karine they had never recruited anyone called Hugo.
The reason for his death almost certainly lies within Marseille's Quartier Nord.
Additional reporting by Marianne Baisnee, Lea Guedj and Paul Pradier

articles.title: Fixing UK’s youth jobs crisis demands much more investment, TUC boss warns
articles.summary:
Paul Nowak also calls on government to avoid arbitrary benefit cuts before much-anticipated Milburn report is published this week

Fixing Britain’s youth jobs crisis will require ministers to…

blocks.text: Fixing Britain’s youth jobs crisis will require ministers to drastically increase investment in employment support while avoiding arbitrary cuts to benefits, the head of the trade union movement has said.

Before an important official report expected next week, the general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, Paul Nowak, said the government had a “once in a generation chance” to secure young people’s futures.

In an interview with the Guardian before the highly anticipated Milburn review into young people and work, he said the costs of increasing job support, education and training would be outweighed by economic gains that would help to ease the pressure on the welfare state.

“There is no solution that is cost-free,” he said. “The government is going to have to be prepared to invest in securing the future of those young people, but also to invest to secure what is the future of our economy.
“This is where the government is going to have to be clear. Of course as a country it’s right to invest in our physical infrastructure, but also we have to invest in social infrastructure too.”

blocks.caption: Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, visits a Boots warehouse in Nottingham to discuss the ‘jobs guarantee’ scheme, which offers subsidised jobs for young people. Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

blocks.text: Ministers are braced for the report by Alan Milburn, the former Labour health secretary, to recommend welfare cuts to fund job support for almost a million young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet).
The report was delayed until after the budget amid fears that the call for welfare cuts would sit uneasily alongside the tax and spending plans of the chancellor, John Healey.

Andy Burnham has said the surge in young people who are Neet is an “economic catastrophe and a moral failure” and that tougher benefits rules and more help for young people will form part of his government’s response to the Milburn report.
after newsletter promotion

The prime minister has been at pains to take a cautious approach to avoid a repeat of the welfare rebellion, which forced Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves into an embarrassing and costly U-turn on planned disability benefit cuts within a year of coming to power.
Calling on Burnham to focus on delivering a step change in employment support, Nowak said increased investment would help to bring down the benefits bill by getting more young people into work.
“We can’t afford to not do this stuff, as the benefits bill will go up if young people are not supported,” he said.

“I don’t think this government is going to repeat the mistake of the previous attempt at benefit reform, where you make arbitrary cuts, [and] where you have an impact on some of the most vulnerable people without thinking about how you support people into work.”

There is rising concern over youth worklessness. Most Britons now see the youth jobs crisis as one of the biggest problems facing the country – ranking it second only to the cost of living and above NHS waiting lists, housing, crime and immigration, according to polling by the research company Focaldata for the Jobs Foundation.

The employment charity, co-founded by the Conservative peer Matthew Elliott, is behind a national campaign to tackle worklessness that launches on Monday. It includes a pledge, backed by a group of leading employers – including Amazon, Pret a Manger, NatWest, Marks & Spencer and Shell – that have committed to support young people who have been overlooked for work.
A government spokesperson said: “We are determined to turn the tide on youth unemployment which has been years in the making.

“We have already pledged £2.5bn in youth employment support, which will deliver almost 500,000 opportunities to earn and learn, while engaging with business including some of Britain’s biggest retail and hospitality brands to create up to 200,000 jobs for young people.
“Further reform will follow the Milburn review, which will be published in the autumn.”

articles.title: Stop undermining Jim Chalmers, environment minister urges Labor colleagues
articles.summary:
‘It’s pretty obvious that there are all sorts of people making all sorts of comments,’ Murray Watt says after budget savings meeting

  • Get our

blocks.text: The environment minister, Murray Watt, has urged ministers to stop undermining the treasurer, Jim Chalmers, as Labor struggles to sell its budget and looks to cut popular clean energy subsidies to help with the fight against inflation.
Cabinet ministers met again on Monday to discuss potential budget savings to be included in next month’s mid-year update, part of efforts to reducing spending to ease pressure on the economy.
Watt was asked about speculation of tension between the treasurer and the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, and whether he’d like to see an end to “undermining and leaking” against Chalmers.

“Yes, I would,” Watt said. “As a member of the government, I take seriously the responsibility to work together to support government policies and also to get our work to support each other in what are very difficult times.

“I think that Jim Chalmers is doing an excellent job as a treasurer in what are very difficult economic times; many of the features that are impacting on our economy are sort of well outside any treasurer’s control, and I very much support Jim Chalmers in his efforts.”
Watt conceded Chalmers was being undermined from within Labor.
“It’s pretty obvious that there are all sorts of people making all sorts of comments.”

A new round of opinion polls added to Labor’s political pain on Monday, with the Resolve Political Monitor in the Age and Sydney Morning Herald showing Labor’s primary vote falling to 28 percentage points, down from 34.6% at last year’s election.
The Coalition also dropped one point to 22%, while One Nation was steady at 25%.
A Redbridge poll in the Financial Review showed Labor’s primary vote slipped two percentage points to 26%, while the Coalition’s jumped four points to 25%. One Nation was down one point to 28%.

Monday’s meeting of the expenditure review committee of cabinet comes after last week’s interest rate hike from the Reserve Bank. The governor, Michele Bullock, said while it is up to governments to manage their budgets independently of the RBA, public and private spending had caused “excess demand” in the economy.
Watt accused the Coalition and minor parties of leaving existing spending proposals to linger in parliament, including savings from changes to the private health insurance rebate for over 65s.
after newsletter promotion

“Let’s not forget that for all of their demands that we find more savings, the Coalition currently are blocking the government from saving $10 billion in measures that are before the parliament,” Watt said.

Albanese has confirmed spending in the public service will be scrutinised as the government looks for savings in the budget update, expected in the middle of December. Last year, departments and agencies were asked to identify potential savings of as much as 5% from their annual budgets, part of the government’s efforts to cut lower-priority spending.
Spending on Labor’s $7bn home battery subsidy program and incentives for electric vehicle purchases could be reined in.
Announced in April 2025, the batteries program was originally designed to cost about $2bn. More than 600,000 systems have been installed, but the program could have means testing rules added.
Separately, subsidies designed to promote uptake of electric vehicles has cost the budget far more than originally anticipated.
Angus Taylor announced an opposition “red tape razor gang” on Monday, designed to reduce the burden on business from costly regulation.

articles.title: Defense witness in Sara Duterte trial grilled on 'all-expense-trip' to China
articles.summary: During the cross-examination, private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. asked Davao City assessor Engineer Jaime Adalin if it was true that he was among the Davao City local government officials who…

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 1:41pm
The first witness presented by the defense was questioned on Monday by the prosecution and some senator-judges about his supposed all-expenses-paid trip to China last year.

During the cross-examination, private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. asked Davao City assessor Engineer Jaime Adalin if it was true that he was among the Davao City local government officials who went to China in November 2025 on an all-expenses-paid tour sponsored by the Chinese consulate.
Defense counsel Lindon Bacquel objected to the question, citing relevance.
Tolosa said the prosecution simply wanted to check the witness’ credibility if he would admit to the matter or not.
“I think that is irrelevant,” Adalin said, drawing laughter from the audience in the session hall.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero also reacted and said, “Funny ka do’n ha (That was funny), Engineer Jimmy.”
Adalin said that he could not recall the date of the trip.
“You cannot recall, sir? If in November 2025, you went to China? Last year? You cannot recall that?” Tolosa asked.
“Your Honor, this is a probing question. I think it’s been clear how evasive this witness has been,” he added.
Bacquel moved to strike Tolosa’s “evasive” remark off the record, but Escudero let it remain.
Senator-Judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III, meanwhile, expressed belief that the question is vital to gauge the credibility of the witness.
“If he doesn’t want to answer, we can always ask the Bureau of Immigration. Simple…then the credibility is proven,” Sotto added.
Escudero then asked Adalin if he could remember traveling to China around November last year.
“Siguro? Again, I don’t have the record. Hindi mo naman memorize ‘yung mga lakad mo ‘no,” the witness answered.
(Maybe? Again, I don’t have the record. You don’t exactly memorize all your travels, right?)
Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo interjected, saying the witness was seemingly fooling around. Tulfo reminded him that he could be cited for contempt for what he is doing.

“Mr. Presiding Officer, para ho tayong niloloko ng testigo na ito. Sir, may I remind you that you're under oath. ‘Yung ginagawa ho ninyong, ginagawa niyong kengkoy ang inyong testimonya, bawal po ‘yan. We can cite you for contempt,” the senator-judge said.

(Mr. Presiding Officer, it feels as though this witness is making us look like fools. Sir, may I remind you that you are under oath. You are turning your testimony into a joke. That is not permitted. We can cite you for contempt.)

“We're serious here. Tinatanong ho kayo, nakapunta ba kayo? Ayaw niyong sabihin. ‘Yung petsa, hindi niyo rin malaman. Kung talagang hindi niyo alam, eh hindi niyo alam. Mr. Presiding Officer, just remind this witness na under oath po siya. ‘Yung pagsisinungaling po eh nasa kanya ho ‘yun, may consequences po ‘yan,” he added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: 'Para tayong niloloko': Sara's first witness warned over China trip answers
articles.summary: Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin first said he could not recall the trip, then said he may have forgotten only the date.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 1:40pm
Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin during the impeachment trial on Nov. 9, 2026.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — The first defense witness in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial drew a contempt warning Monday, November 9 after giving shifting answers when asked whether he had taken an all-expense-paid trip to China.
During cross-examination, prosecution lawyer Benjamin Tolosa asked Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin about the trip as part of an attempt to test his credibility.
"Actually, hindi ko talaga ma-recall," Adalin initially said. ("Actually, I really cannot recall.")
Defense counsel Lindon Bacquel objected to the question. But Adalin, a witness, stepped over the line when he himself called it "irrelevant."
Senator-Judge Vicente Sotto III intervened, saying the Bureau of Immigration could be asked to verify the trip if Adalin refused to answer.
"I believe that question is important to gauge the credibility of the witness," Sotto said.
Presiding Officer Francis Escudero then pressed Adalin on whether he could not remember the trip itself or merely its date.
"Ah, siguro ang petsa, sir," Adalin replied. ("Ah, probably the date, sir.")
Asked whether he had traveled to China around the period in question, Adalin said: "Ah, siguro. Because again, I don't have the record. Hindi mo na ma-memorize 'yung mga lakad mo ano?"
("Ah, probably. Because again, I don't have the record. You can't really memorize all your trips, right?")
Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo then warned Adalin about his shifting answers and reminded him he was testifying under oath.
"Mr. Presiding Officer, para ho tayong niloloko ng testigo na ito," Tulfo said. ("Mr. Presiding Officer, it feels like this witness is making fools out of us.")
"Sir, may I remind you that you're under oath? Kung ginagawa ninyong kenkoy ang inyong testimonio, bawal po iyan. We can cite you for contempt," he added.
("Sir, may I remind you that you're under oath? If you are making a joke out of your testimony, that is not allowed. We can cite you for contempt.")

As assessor in Duterte's hometown, Adalin was called to court to testify for the defense as it began presenting counter-evidence on Article II of impeachment charges against the vice president. The article covers her alleged unexplained wealth.
An assessor is in charge of classifying and appraising the value of all real estate properties within a jurisdiction.

articles.title: Witness: Romualdez, Co proponents for P27-B DPWH projects per Cabral's instructions
articles.summary: Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez and former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co were identified as proponents of P27 billion worth of projects under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) upon…

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 1:38pm

Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez and former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co were identified as proponents of P27 billion worth of projects under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) upon the instructions of the late Undersecretary Catalina Cabral, a prosecution witness said Monday.

Engineer Peter Paul Cortez, chief of the DPWH Programming Division, made the testimony during the bail hearing of Romualdez, who is facing a P7.4 billion plunder case alongside Co, Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.
Cortez said his division “assumed” that Romualdez and Co were proponents of the P27 billion since their names were given by Cabral to be encoded in the DPWH database.
Cabral died in December 2025 in an apparent fall into a ravine in Benguet.

Asked by Sandiganbayan Third Division Chairperson Justice Karl Miranda as to why he identified Romualdez and Co as the project proponents in his judicial affidavit, Cortez replied “Per record of our database, they are the ones tagged as proponents. Actually, our term there is inserted.”
The P27 billion worth of projects were not proposed by the DPWH under the National Expenditure Program but were part of congressional amendments that made it to the General Appropriations Act.
Cortez said his "best guess" was that the amendments were made at the bicameral conference committee deliberations, the panel which reconciles the House and Senate versions of the proposed budget.
During the cross-examination by Romualdez’s counsel, Atty. Felix Villa, Cortez said he did not talk to the lawmaker or his staff regarding the projects.
Likewise, Cortez said that Cabral’s instructions as to identifying proponents were not documented, and that the database of the DPWH did not indicate commissions.
Romualdez has repeatedly denied his involvement in the alleged kickback scheme in flood control projects. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
articles.summary: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV has said Argentina's economy must benefit everyone including the poor, in a diplomatic but pointed critique of President Javier Milei's austerity measures.
The Pope was speaking as he arrived in Buenos Aires, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, only three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.
In response, right-wing leader Milei said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today".

This leg of the Pope's journey was expected be the most politically sensitive, with the president's agenda of slashing public spending having been denounced by the Catholic Church for hitting the poorest hardest.
"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," Pope Leo said.

He stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs", and urged that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.
In what appeared to be a rebuke of Milei's combative style and language, the Pope said strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words".
Milei had been particularly outspoken about Leo's predecessor Pope Francis, whom he called "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor.
On Sunday, however, Milei struck a conciliatory tone, calling Francis an "exceptional figure" and "undoubtedly the most important Argentine in history".
He was also keen to welcome the current Pope earlier, writing in a post on X that Argentina awaits "with immense joy".

Pope Leo urged Argentina to safeguard its democracy. "Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community," he said.

In his own address welcoming Leo to Argentina, Milei defended his libertarian policies, saying the rights to life, liberty and property are the backbone of Argentina's constitution and of Western democracies.
The Argentine leader, who has said he will seek re-election next year, is a strong supporter of US President Donald Trump, who has criticised Pope Leo for his opposition to the Iran war.
Pope Leo's trip to Argentina has been described as a homage to Francis, who did not return to his homeland during his own papacy.

The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition".
Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

articles.title: Gasoline, diesel get big rollbacks on November 10
articles.summary: Motorists will get some relief after months of expensive fuel, as global oil prices fall on hopes of easing Middle East tensions

blocks.text: INCREASE. Another round of fuel price adjustments takes effect in Manila, on April 7, 2026.
Rappler
Motorists will get some relief after months of expensive fuel, as global oil prices fall on hopes of easing Middle East tensions
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are set for a bigtime rollback starting Tuesday, November 10.
The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following permitted price adjustments for November 10 to 16:

items: Gasoline – rollback of at least P16.80 per liter
Diesel – rollback of at least P4.10 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of at least P3.70 per liter

blocks.caption: FUEL ROLLBACK. Screenshot from DOE’s press conference on Monday, November 9.

blocks.text: Last week, gasoline prices saw a hike of as much as P3.50 per liter, while diesel and kerosene prices fell by at least P1 and P1.90 per liter, respectively.

International oil prices fell as hope rekindled for the easing of tensions between the United States and Iran following the US midterm elections. A possible de-escalation of the conflict could allow more Middle Eastern oil to reach global markets, improving the strained supply.

Local pump prices remain substantially higher than before fighting involving Iran and US-Israeli forces broke out on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at P56 per liter for RON95 gasoline, P54.70 for RON91, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene.
The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates.

Meanwhile, excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene remain suspended under Executive Order No. 125, issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in September. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Macalintal to seek SC reconsideration of BSKE ruling
articles.summary: Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal on Monday said he would file a motion for reconsideration (MR) of the Supreme Court's decision upholding the law that postponed the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan…

blocks.text: Published November 9, 2026 1:02pm

Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal on Monday said he would file a motion for reconsideration (MR) of the Supreme Court's decision upholding the law that postponed the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) and extended the term of incumbent barangay officials.
"Ako'y maghahain ng motion for reconsideration at iyan ay pinapayagan sa ating rules," Macalintal told Super Radyo dzBB.
(I will file a motion for reconsideration, which is allowed under our rules.)
Macalintal said he plans to file the motion this week.
"Inaayos ko na lamang yung presentation, yung format ng gagawin ko whether to ask for a total MR or a partial MR na kung saan bibigyan ko ng win-win formula ang ating SC sa bagay na ito," he said.
(I'm just finalizing the presentation and format of my motion, whether to seek a full or partial reconsideration, in which I will offer the SC a win-win formula.)

He said he may ask the SC to uphold its ruling that declared unconstitutional the provision of Republic Act No. 12326 granting Congress the authority to fix the term of office, while maintaining its ruling on the provision postponing the elections.

"Maaari natin sabihin sa SC na 'okay, you declared unconstitutional yung RA 12326 na nagbibigay ng kapangyarihan na to fix the term of office' pero declared naman na unconstitutional yung bahaging nagpo-postpone ng halalan" so parehong panalo. Panalo ang kongreso, panalo ang tao," he added.

(We can tell the SC that it declared unconstitutional the provision of RA 12326 granting the authority to fix the term of office, while also declaring unconstitutional the portion postponing the elections. That way, both sides win. Congress wins, and the people win.)
In a 33-page decision, the SC dismissed Macalintal's petition challenging the constitutionality of the law.

The High Court said the law's primary purpose was to fix the term of office rather than postpone the elections. It also ruled that the guidelines established in its 2023 decision on a petition filed by Macalintal did not apply to the case.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Republic Act No. 12326 into law in September, effectively postponing the BSKE, setting the term of office of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials at five years and moving the next elections to 2028.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Burnham’s homelessness pledge to ‘get everyone in for Christmas’ in jeopardy
articles.summary:
Minister says Labour hoping to offer bed to every rough sleeper in England but cites chronic housing shortage

Andy Burnham’s pledge to tackle rough sleeping by getting “everyone in for…
articles.byline: Josh Halliday North of England editor

blocks.text: Andy Burnham’s pledge to tackle rough sleeping by getting “everyone in for Christmas” is in jeopardy amid rising numbers of people on the streets and a severe housing shortage.
Official figures show an increase of nearly 1,000 people sleeping rough in England between January and June, the latest month for which figures are available.
There were 8,748 rough sleepers in England in June, the highest number since November 2025, according to government statistics.
Only 15% of those were found accommodation by the end of June, the lowest level since August 2025 as councils struggle with the growing demand for temporary and affordable housing.
The homelessness minister, Florence Eshalomi, said the government hoped to offer a bed to every rough sleeper by Christmas but that there was a chronic shortage of suitable housing.

Asked whether every person on the streets in England would be offered accommodation in the next six weeks, she said: “We’re hoping to offer that, but what we are definitely offering is a route off the street for everyone who wants to take up that offer.”
A “route off the street” may not necessarily involve housing, Eshalomi said.
“For some people it will be a route into accommodation, for some people it could be a … dedicated plan around their mental health or substance misuse, so that’s what we are committed to.
“The offer of a bed will be there for people who want that. We cannot force people off the streets – we’ve got to respect that as well – but that offer will be there.”

blocks.caption: The homelessness minister, Florence Eshalomi Photograph: Alamy Live News.

blocks.text: Burnham has pledged to offer every rough sleeper in England a safe route off the streets or wider support as a central part of his premiership.

Councils across England have said the number of homeless families is growing as a result of the chronic shortage of affordable housing, record demand for temporary accommodation and the long-term freeze of local housing allowance, meaning rents far outstrip the welfare available to those on low incomes.

Frontline professionals are also concerned about the impact of the prisons early release scheme, with some offenders being released without stable accommodation, as well as a flood of no-fault evictions before the practice was banned on 1 May.

A record 135,600 households in England were living in temporary accommodation such as B&Bs and hostels at the end of March 2026, according to official figures. This is about 90% higher than a decade ago and 4% higher than the previous year.

In a speech in Downing Street when he became prime minister on 20 July, Burnham said: “I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction: to end rough sleeping in our country.”
after newsletter promotion
The next month, he announced increased funding of £442m as part of what he called the “national drive to get everyone in for Christmas”.
In October he set out a further £432m in funding from March 2027 so that people would be “offered a safe route off the streets this winter” and support to the end of this parliament.
Eshalomi, who was appointed by Burnham in July, previously described the freeze of local housing allowance as one of the “systemic barriers” and a “big sticking point” in reducing homelessness.
Speaking on a visit to a temporary accommodation facility in Manchester last week, she said the area was not “best policy” and that she raised it “constantly with colleagues … with the Treasury”.
Asked whether she raised it with fellow ministers before John Healey’s budget last month, she said: “I’ve been an MP since 2019. I’ve been raising it since then.”
Eshalomi said she was working with councils and housing associations in England to bring thousands of empty or derelict properties into use to help tackle rough sleeping.
She said ultimately the solution was “building those homes”.

“It’s around making sure we’re building more social and affordable homes so that people don’t have to find themselves choosing between not having enough money and support to live in a private rented sector.”

articles.title: Starbucks plans to hire 7,500 staff in major UK expansion plan
articles.summary:
Coffee shop chain targets growth north of London with extra 500 outlets in big boost for youth employment

Starbucks has set out plans to hire 7,500 new baristas over the next five years, in…

blocks.text: Starbucks has set out plans to hire 7,500 new baristas over the next five years, in a boost to youth employment as the chain pins hopes for future growth on the north of the country.

The US coffee shop chain, which employs more than 18,000 people in the UK, said the hiring spree would focus on the Midlands, north of England, Wales and Scotland, as it targets growth north of the M25.

The roles are expected to staff 500 new coffee shops which Starbucks hopes to open across the country by 2031. The company set out the growth plan earlier this year after shutting dozens of underperforming outlets in Britain last year as part of a $1bn (£750m) global restructuring.
Darren King, who runs Starbucks UK, said: “We’re deeply focused on how we can help more young people into these positions, starting by making entry-level roles as accessible as possible.”

Starbucks is a large youth employer and set out its plan before an official report into the number of young people not in education, employment or training, known as Neets, which hit a record high above 1 million at the start of the year.

The rise in worklessness was dealt a blow in the run-up to the budget last month, as UK employers cut back on hiring amid worries about rising costs and the outlook for the British economy, according to a monthly survey.

The number of people taking up permanent jobs across the UK fell for the first time in four months, according to the latest jobs report from KPMG and the Recruitment & Employment Confederation, compiled by S&P Global. Recruitment for temporary roles also fell, for the first time since March.

Jon Holt, the chief executive and UK senior partner of KPMG, said: “October saw employers pull back on hiring in the month leading up to the budget, ending a run of more positive news over recent months. Renewed geopolitical and economic uncertainty weighed on confidence, with further energy price shocks and a global bond sell-off pushing borrowing costs higher.”

Holt added: “Businesses will now be assessing whether the measures announced in the budget give them enough stability to absorb the external pressures and higher costs they face. But with the Bank of England increasing interest rates and inflation set to continue rising over the coming months, there is a risk the green shoots we had been seeing in the jobs market could stall.”
after newsletter promotion
Separate analysis by the Resolution Foundation found that job satisfaction among UK workers is at a record low, amid a lack of flexible working, insecure jobs and a loss of independence.

articles.title: Robredo rules out presidential run anew: 'It's really closed'
articles.summary: The Naga mayor says her decision not to return to national politics came with her 2025 mayoral run and cannot be changed.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 12:56pm
Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo speaks at a local event on Tuesday, Nov. 18, 2025.
Leni Gerona Robredo via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo again ruled out a run for the presidency in 2028 a year before the filing of candidacies, saying the matter was now "closed" and that she lacked the political savvy needed to navigate national politics.
Robredo said she had settled the matter before running for mayor in 2025, and would not return to national office even if she later decided to leave City Hall.
"It's really closed. Nothing can change that," Robredo said in Bikol in a radio interview on Monday, November 9.
Robredo has resolved not to use the mayoralty as a stepping stone toward 2028. "When I ran for mayor, that decision came with it, that I would no longer leave Naga."
Robredo first ruled out a run for the presidency in April in an interview with the same radio station, RMN dwNX Naga, saying she would most likely seek a second term as mayor instead.
Opposition figures, including Sen. Kiko Pangilinan, her 2022 running mate, have since urged her to reconsider.
Early polling for 2028 presidential bets has placed Robredo as a potential frontrunner second to Vice President Sara Duterte, who remains ahead in the surveys.
In a Pulse Asia survey conducted September 17 to 24, which tested a wide field of possible candidates, Duterte was the preference of 50% of those surveyed, while Robredo was at 26%.

Asked about Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon, whose repeated trips to Naga have fed speculation about a 2028 tandem, Robredo said: "[Secretary] Vince has never brought up 2028." She said his visits were tied to the work they had done together in the city.

Dizon has been in Naga several times this year, the most recent being an unannounced visit on October 26, the same day Malacañang moved him from the Department of Public Works and Highways back to the Department of Transportation in a swap with Secretary Giovanni "Banoy" Lopez. Neither side disclosed what was discussed. Dizon has denied that his visits carry a political agenda.

Robredo also said she had not spoken with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. about 2028. She said her last conversation with him was at his birthday celebration in Malacañang in September, which she attended on invitation along with other local chief executives.
The former vice president was also candid in explaining how her years in both national and local office had shown her where she falls short.
"Maybe I could handle the job, but my political savvy really seems lacking," she said. "At the national level, you need to be a strong communicator. I'm weak at that."
She said the next president should be able "not only to do the job but also to handle national politics."
"At the national level, people largely believe what they read, how you're portrayed," she said. In Naga, she said she believes she could better focus on the work without having to play politics.
Robredo served as vice president from 2016 to 2022 after defeating Marcos for the post. She lost the 2022 presidential election to him, receiving 14.8 million votes to his 31 million.
In May 2025, she was elected Naga's first female mayor.

articles.title: [EDITORIAL] Lessons from the ‘blue wave’
articles.summary: Pragmatism over ideology, grassroots organizing, at economic and food stability ang nagpapanalo ng eleksiyon.

blocks.text: Pragmatism over ideology, grassroots organizing, at economic and food stability ang nagpapanalo ng eleksiyon.
Parang storm surge ang epekto sa Pilipinas ng “blue wave” ng US Democrats kung saan inilampaso nila ang Republicans ni US President Donald Trump — nakakagulantang, at oo, nakaka-high.
Pero simple lang ang muling pinatunayan ng outcome ng midterms: people vote with their stomachs.
Dito sa Pilipinas, nangahas na naman tayong mangarap, at hindi natin maiaalis na mangarap ang oposisyon ng isang “pink wave.”

Pero bago muling magtayo ng mga kastilyo sa buhangin, suriin muna natin ang blue wave. Hindi naman biglang na-in love ang American voters sa Democrats, lalo na’t sariwa pa sa alaala ng voters ang age-related issues at family drama ni dating pangulong si Joe Biden. Pagod na lang sila sa nagtataasang presyo ng gas at groceries, at kawalan ng magandang trabaho. At lalong pagod na sila sa foreign wars na ipinangako ni Trump noong eleksiyon na hinding-hindi niya papasukin.
Kapag taghirap, nagiging balota ang hapag-kainan.

‘Yan ang leksiyon na tila hindi natutunan ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Bago pa naganap ang War on Iran ng Estados Unidos, runaway inflation na ang idinadaing ng mga Pilipino. Ito rin ang isa sa mga dahilan kung bakit kalahati lamang ang naipanalo ni Marcos sa slate niya noong 2025 midterms.

Ano ba ang blind spot ng oposisyon? Sabi ni Rappler columnist Joey Salgado, lagi na lang “disente” ang naratibong ibinabandera ng Liberals, at andiyan pa rin daw ang sakit na “talking down” sa mga botante.
Kung galit ang mga pemenista sa “mansplaining,” asar ang mahihirap sa “richsplaining.”

To be clear, mahalagang bahagi ng legislative agenda ng matinong pulitiko ang panunumbalik ng respeto sa karapatang pantao, gender rights, at good governance. Pero, sadly, hindi ito ang mga isyung magdadala sa mga botante sa polling precinct. Bituka pa rin ang mangingibabaw.

At napag-uusapan din lang ang “richsplaining,” priceless ang kakayanang makinig nang buong pagpapakumbaba sa pangkaraniwang tao. Habang may oras at lugar para ipaliwanag ang mga konsepto ng kalayaan, human rights, at demokrasya, kailangan munang makinig ang pulitiko sa hinaing ng constituents niya.
The Dutertes built their political clout on relatability and the ability to speak the language of the masses. It’s also a skill that can be acquired by the pinks and liberals.

Maliban sa kapalpakan ni Trump, ‘yan din ang nagpapanalo sa US Democrats kahit na sa traditional strongholds ng Republicans: paulit-ulit nilang pinagdiinan ang “pocketbook” issues na malapit sa puso ng mga botante.
Pagkatapos ng gut issues, kailangang magbuo ang oposisyon ng base labas sa usual friends. Crucial ang alliance building, lalo na kung ang pundasyon ay gut issues at good governance.
To recap: pragmatism over ideology, grassroots organizing, at economic and food stability ang nagpapanalo ng eleksiyon.

Makapangyarihan ang boto mo. Hindi lamang doleouts o ayuda ang dapat bitbit nito, kundi tunay na public service at tangible change. Kalsadang namimintina. Flood control na nagpapahupa ng baha at hindi nagpapayaman sa contractor at pulitiko. Police visibility at pagpuksa ng kriminalidad nang hindi nauuwi sa mass murder. Jobs creation and livelihood training. Medical clinics at free health services. Educational assistance.

‘Yan ang pinakamahalagang leksiyon ng isang electoral wave para sa unaligned majority — para sa jeepney driver na halos walang kinikita nang nagtaasan ang presyo ng krudo; para sa call center employee na madi-displace dahil sa AI technology; para sa laborer na walang trabaho dahil sa shrinkage ng construction sector.
May boses tayo. Puwede nating palitan ang nakaupo, ang kalakaran, kahit ang balanse ng kapangyarihan sa pagitan ng mayaman at mahirap. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Victorian election 2026: Concern and scepticism among Labor MPs as new poll shows party trailing One Nation
articles.summary:
Ben Carroll refuses to be drawn on latest opinion poll that puts Labor at all-time low of just 18%, behind One Nation on 21% and the Coalition on 33%

  • Get our

blocks.text: Victorian Labor MPs are both sceptical and seriously concerned about a new poll ahead of the state election showing the party trailing third behind One Nation, with its primary vote at an all-time low of just 18%.

The DemosAU/PremierNational, first published by the Herald Sun on Monday, showed Labor’s primary vote share has crashed seven points to 18%, putting it in third place behind the Coalition’s 33% and One Nation’s 21%. At the same time, the Greens improved their primary vote to 17%, an increase of three points since September.
It means the Coalition now leads Labor on a two-party preferred basis 56-44, compared with 52-48 in September.

DemosAU’s head of research, George Hasanakos, said if the poll were replicated on election night, many contests across the state would be between the Liberals or Nationals and One Nation, which would then result in a “clear Coalition majority”.
“If that happens, One Nation has to poll really, really well to have a chance of winning, because Labor and Greens preferences will flow to the Liberals,” he said.

On election night, the Victorian electoral commission plans to conduct a two-candidate-preferred count, or 2CP, between the two candidates it expects to finish with the most support after preferences are distributed. They are selecting the indicative 2CP for each seat based on on polling, analysis of preference flows and results from previous, which will not publish this before election day to avoid influencing voter behaviour.
Hasanakos added that he “double, triple, quadruple checked” the result of the “extraordinary” poll, which had 1,562 respondents, an effective sample of 818 and a margin of error of 3.4%.
“We went to the trouble of a bigger sample here, and I stand by it,” he said.
Ben Carroll repeatedly refused to say whether he was worried about the poll at a press conference in South Melbourne on Monday morning.

“What I’m focused on every day is fighting for working people and making sure that every Victorian that goes into the ballot on November 28 knows that under my government you have a government on your side that will fight for you,” he told reporters.
“The alternative is a Liberal-One Nation government that will fight against you – they’re going to shrink the economy, cause a recession and make life difficult for every single Victorian.”

But the result has sparked serious concerns among the Labor caucus, even though some MPs are sceptical about the 18% figure. Inside Labor’s campaign headquarters, they are treating the result as an “outlier” and point to other public polls that have their primary vote in the 20s.
Several Labor MPs, unauthorised to speak publicly, have told Guardian Australia there are many in the caucus questioning their party’s strategy.

This includes a focus in recent days on crime – an issue that is typically a Coalition strength. On Sunday, Carroll announced a $204m plan to enable judges to sentence low- and mid-level youth offenders to a new rehabilitation detention program while on Monday he announced $70m to recruit 200 more police reservists to re-open stations and build and upgrade more stations.
after newsletter promotion
“Caucus is really angry and deflated, because this is all happening because of him,” one MP
“Even if it’s higher than 18, and we get back into something with a 2 in front of it, the experiment has been an epic fail, the campaign is in freefall, and it’s about to get a whole lot worse.”
Another MP said the focus on crime was “diabolically stupid strategy” as the government had years to tackle community concern around rising rates.

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, on Monday said her party had a focus on “getting tough on crime”, including by introducing Aidan’s Law, to toughen sentencing for attacks on people who step in to protect others.

Carroll immediately matched the commitment to introduce the proposed law, named after 22-year-old Aidan Becker, who was fatally stabbed at Mernda station after stepping in to protect a 14-year-old during an alleged violent robbery.
It comes as Pauline Hanson rejected reports by The Age and 60 Minutes on Sunday that her former national campaign director, Sean Black, continues to secretly work for One Nation in Victoria.

Black was in 2018 was jailed for rape and subsequently lost his appeal against the conviction but was then rehired by One Nation in 2020 as a campaign director after serving his time. Hanson sacked him after political pressure earlier this year.
She told the Australian Financial Review on Monday “the day that I sacked him [Sean Black] that was the day he finished up”.

PAGASA
Typhoon Samuel (Cempaka) will only stay briefly inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility

items: Typhoon Cempaka, locally named Samuel, entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility but is not expected to affect the country.
The northeast monsoon is causing rain in several areas and dangerous sea conditions.
